Hughesville.wildlife_intro:
Hughesville hosts the Lycoming County Fair, and the rest of the year it is Wolf Township farm country with a borough in the middle. Groundhogs own the fence lines here — our crew is called for burrows at barn foundations, equipment sheds, and garden edges more than for any other single problem. Raccoons move between those same barns and the borough's chimneys as the seasons turn, bats roost in the older Main Street attics, and skunks den under porches on the quiet residential streets behind the fairgrounds. Muncy Creek, just west of the borough, keeps the whole rotation supplied.

Timing matters in Hughesville. Spring opening reveals a winter's worth of quiet damage in seasonal homes, raccoon litters fill chimneys and attics, and summer bat colonies raise young in the older rooflines — with exclusions held, per Pennsylvania Game Commission guidance, outside the May 15 through August 1 maternity window. Skunks and groundhogs work the yards until frost, and fall sends rodents and squirrels into heated buildings for the long winter. Our crew times the work to the animal and the season, and seals every entry we find.
